chains.title: TCF7L2 ref-preferred binding at an 8q24 enhancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 is the strongest TF candidate: it occupies the variant in HCT116 ChIP-seq and is highly expressed, and QBiC-SELEX reports ref-preferred binding (effect -0.429, z -8.8); however the QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped TCF7, not a TCF7L2 own model, and bulk ChIP does not prove allele-specific occupancy.

rs73706717 lies in the active proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 marked by DNase, H3K27ac, and TF occupancy, although the cCRE z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples rather than HCT116-specific.

POU5F1B is the nearest protein-coding gene and the best L2G gene in the supplied credible sets, but those sets are for non-CRC traits with low PIP, no GTEx eQTL links this base to POU5F1B, and MYC is a farther but known 8q24 CRC oncogene, so target assignment is uncertain.
HCT116 is the matching colorectal carcinoma biosample; TCF7L2 is expressed at 63.61 TPM and HCT116 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.

A TCF7L2-dependent enhancer change could alter 8q24 target expression in colorectal cells, but rs73706717 has no GWAS Catalog association and no colorectal-cancer genetic link is supplied, so the phenotype step is speculative.

predictions: The alt C allele reduces TCF7L2 binding at rs73706717.
If TCF7L2 activates this enhancer, alt C reduces target-gene expression in HCT116.
TCF7L2 knockdown should reduce enhancer activity if this element is TCF7L2-dependent.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP does not show ref>T occupancy at rs73706717 in HCT116.
Reporter assays show no differential enhancer activity between T and C alleles.
TCF7L2 knockdown or CRISPRi does not affect the relevant 8q24 target gene in HCT116.

chains.title: SP1 ref-preferred binding at the same enhancer

The variant is in the active pELS EH38E3858447, consistent with an SP1-bound regulatory element, though the cCRE annotation is not HCT116-specific.
POU5F1B is nearest and top L2G in the supplied non-CRC credible sets, but there is no GTEx eQTL and no direct SP1-to-POU5F1B enhancer evidence, so the target-gene link is weak.
HCT116 expresses SP1 at 38.96 TPM and has SP1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.
A change in SP1 occupancy at this 8q24 enhancer could alter colorectal-cell gene regulation, but no supplied evidence links rs73706717 or SP1 at this element to colorectal cancer.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr8:127401265:T>C, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000971), bound here before bound elsewhere, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 40 occupied, 5 of 103 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 11 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 517 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 5 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly.
